result.abstractText: Machine learning can unlock genomic selection (GS) for polygenic traits, but only if millions of SNPs are distilled into breeder-actionable loci. Here, we presented genome-wide association signal ranking with linkage disequilibrium pruning and Random Forest feature importance selection (GLRS), a trait-informed framework for deriving ultra-sparse marker sets for pure-line and hybrid GS breeding in wheat. Training on 768 diverse accessions phenotyped for nine yield-related traits across six environments and 570,441 SNPs, GLRS compressed markers for each trait to a few hundred yet raised cross-validation accuracy by 7.2% relative to conventional GS using random selected markers. Independent evaluation using a publicly available wheat dataset further supported the robustness and general applicability of the GLRS strategy. Validation in 1,163 advanced breeding lines from seven independent trials further demonstrated the robustness of GLRS, with prediction accuracy improvement of 14.4% and 5.8% over random markers and genome-wide association signal ranking with linkage disequilibrium pruning markers, respectively. GLRS also delivered accurate predictions of F<sub>1</sub> performance (r = 0.790), general combining ability (r = 0.851) and heterosis (r = 0.541) in 292 hybrid combinations, enabling simultaneous hybrid wheat and elite inbred variety development. Finally, we proposed a combining-ability-based GS strategy for wheat pure-line and hybrid breeding. This study provided an efficient GLRS pipeline to facilitate the practical application of trait-informed GS in wheat high-yield breeding.

result.abstractText:
Short summary

TeroSeek is an AI-powered platform that converts terpenoid literature into a structured knowledge base of over 3 million entries and an expert Q&A agent. By coupling knowledge-graph retrieval with large language models, it delivers evidence-based, fully cited answers that reduce hallucination and bypass knowledge cutoffs. The framework is readily transferable to other scientific domains.

result.abstractText: Geng rice (Oryza sativa subsp. japonica) from northeast China dominates the country's high-value rice market because of its superior eating quality. However, current methods for quality evaluation rely on either labor-intensive, subjective sensory protocols or low-accuracy, calibration-heavy near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), thus hindering breeding efforts for high eating quality and market development. Here, we report a vision-based deep learning framework that combines multi-population fine-tuning with industrial vision-language model (VLM) pre-training to predict the eating quality of Geng rice. Trained on datasets from natural and recombinant inbred (RI) populations, our optimal model (Model 4) showed high cross-population stability. It achieved R<sup>2</sup> values of 0.98 for a natural-population validation set (35 cultivars), 0.57 for the independent DA-RI population (201 lines), and 0.61 for a randomly collected set of 30 cultivars from northeast China and 28 cultivars from southern China, consistently outperforming the widely used Satake STA1B analyzer. This approach also enabled us to map a novel, robust quantitative trait locus, qIVOE7, for Geng rice eating quality on chromosome 7. Further analysis suggested that Model 4 relied primarily on the hue dimension of the HSV (hue, saturation, and value) color space for its predictions. This framework provides a highly accurate predictive model and a simple tool for the evaluation of rice eating quality, helping to accelerate the breeding and market development of high-quality rice.
